The proposal lists only Cost Per Delivery.","evidence_quote":"Cost Per Delivery: must not increase.","citations":["guardrail-standards#eta-and-delivery-promise-changes"],"recommendation":"Add Delivery CSAT, Contact Rate and Promise Accuracy as guardrails, each with a stop threshold. Conversion should also be tracked, given the EXP-014 result."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Customer-level randomization, 1-week duration, no MDE/power","detail":"Randomizing by customer leaks effects between arms because promises share one supply pool. One week is under the 14-day minimum, and no MDE, sample size/power or stopping rule is recorded.","evidence_quote":"A/B test randomized by customer. Run for 1 week.","citations":["experimentation-standards#marketplace-interference","experimentation-standards#duration-and-seasonality","experimentation-standards#pre-registration"],"recommendation":"Use a switchback, geo or zone-level design. Run at least 14 days, or get Data Science sign-off for a shorter test. Pre-register the primary metric, MDE, power and stopping rule."},{"type":"PRIOR_ART","title":"EXP-014 referenced but its learning not applied","detail":"EXP-014 (padded promise windows) was concluded and not shipped. The OTD gain came from relaxed promises and conversion fell 1.2%. The proposal cites it but judges success on On-Time Delivery Rate alone, which is the pitfall the learning warns against.","evidence_quote":"Follows EXP-014, but only applies during storms rather than permanently.","citations":["experiment-registry#exp-014-eta-buffer"],"recommendation":"State the EXP-014 outcome and explain why the storm-only scope should avoid the conversion loss.
